verdict.reasoning: Patient reports lower abdominal pain in the middle, below the belly button, constant, for a few days, worsening, rated 8/10: “I'm having really bad tummy egg… at the lower bottom of my belly… it's like lower… in the middle… Below [belly button]… It's there all the time… A few days ago… it's kind of really getting worse with time… Maybe 8.”

Transcript confirms light pink bleeding after menses but does not specify that it started “approximately two weeks after the last menstrual period”; timing of onset of the light bleeding relative to LMP is not clearly stated: “my period stopped like last two weeks ago. And this is different… it's just light pink color.”
Patient explicitly reports nausea without vomiting: “I feel nausea. Like, I feel like vomiting, but I don't. I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.”
Patient had constipation last week, now improved with daily BMs: “Like I was constipated for a week… this week it seems to be… It's fine now… Are you going to the toilet every day? Patient: Yeah.”
Patient notes reduced urinary frequency: “I don't really. I have noticed that I don't really go often like before. So, yeah, I do. I do drink a lot though.”

She denies urinary pain, odor, and urgency: Doctor asks, “Any pain or strong smell or having to go more often than normal?” Patient’s only comment is decreased frequency, not pain/odor/urgency, which implies denial of those symptoms.

She denies SOB, shoulder pain, fever, and presyncope: “Any difficulty breathing or pain in your shoulders or anything like that? Patient: No. No.”; “Do you feel feverish? Patient: No.”; “Do you feel faint when you stand up? Patient: No.”
She is tolerating oral intake: “have you been eating and drinking? Okay. Patient: Yeah, yeah, my regular activities and drinking and other things. Okay.”

She continues normal work and home activities: “What have you been doing for the last few days? Have you been at work as normal or had to stay at home? Patient: Yes, I have been. I'm doing. I work other activities like cooking and stuff. It seems okay.”
LMP 2–3 weeks ago is stated: “When was your last period? … about two weeks. Three weeks ago.”
Sexual activity and last intercourse 4 days ago: “Are you having sexual intercourse regularly? Patient: Yes… Four weeks ago. Four days ago. Sorry, I just had.”

Pregnancy test was one month ago and not repeated since pain onset: “Have you taken a pregnancy test this time? Patient: Yeah, I did. … Doctor: When was that? Patient: Yeah, around like a month ago. Doctor: Okay, but not since you've had the abdominal pain.”

Patient reports an allergy (likely a drug allergy though drug not fully clear): “Have you had any other medical problems in the past? Patient: Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy… Ammo. Excellent allergy.”

She is using Implanon for contraception for about a year: “Are you using any contraception? Patient: Yes, I am. I use it from last one year. Plan on calling. Plan… Doctor: And your Implanon was just put in a year ago? Patient: Yes.”

Implanon is clearly an ongoing contraceptive (current medication): “Are you using any contraception? … I use it from last one year… Doctor: And your Implanon was just put in a year ago? Patient: Yes.”
A drug allergy is reported but drug name is unclear: “Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy… Ammo. Excellent allergy.” The specific agent is not intelligible.
Employment as a teacher: “And what's your job day to day? Patient: Yeah, I'm a teacher.”
Living with husband and his family: “And who do you live with at home? Patient: My husband and my husband's family.”
Denies tobacco, alcohol, and drugs: “And do you smoke or drink alcohol? You take any other drugs? Patient: No.”
Travel abroad one year ago: “Have you been abroad recently? Patient: Yes. … Doctor: Oh, a year ago. Not recently? Patient: No.”
No prior pregnancies: “Have you had any pregnancies? Patient: No.” Gravida 0 is a direct inference.

Irregular menses on implant: “And do you have your periods when you. Since you've been using the Implanon, do you have periods? Patient: Yes, ideally. Doctor: Or are they sporadic? Patient: No, they are sporadic. Like not the time it changes.”

All components appear in the history: acute lower midline pain below umbilicus, 8/10, few days, worsening (“A few days… really getting worse… Maybe 8”); light post‑menses bleeding (“my period stopped like last two weeks ago. And this is different… light pink color”); on Implanon, sexually active, pregnancy status unknown (last test a month ago); nausea without vomiting; prior constipation now improved.
Face‑to‑face review for abdominal exam is arranged: “we can arrange a face to face examination where they can see you in a clinic and do an abdominal examination and advise further from them.”
Plan to obtain pregnancy test today: “The other thing we would need to do is to do a pregnancy test today if possible. So if you can do that today…”
Immediate review if test positive: “…if it's positive, we need to see you straight away. So give us a call back.”

Advice to seek earlier/urgent review if pain worsens or cannot keep fluids down: “In the meantime, if it gets a lot worse or you. You're not holding any fluids down, then we should see you before then.”

Patient is to call support line to book appointment: “Would you be happy to call the support line and arrange that appointment? … if you call the support line and make an appointment, we'll go from there.”
